expect: ~7 million metric tons of reserves x ~70% mining efficiency x ~40% directed to batteries = ~2 million metric tons (p1.L42-47, Fig. 1 caption)
question: How does the review get from the known global cobalt reserves to the cobalt usable for batteries, and what amount results?
rendered:
According to the review, the known global cobalt reserves are approximately 7 million metric tons. To calculate the cobalt usable for batteries, the review assumes a conservative mining efficiency of ≈70% and that ≈40% of the mined cobalt is directed toward battery manufacturing. 

Calculation:
Cobalt usable for batteries = (Cobalt reserves x Mining efficiency x Percentage directed toward battery manufacturing)
= (7,000,000 metric tons x 0.7 x 0.4)
= 2,000,000 metric tons

So, the review estimates that approximately 2 million metric tons of cobalt are usable for battery manufacturing.
